findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume, snapshots and logs holding application data are stored unencrypted.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing MySQL to untrusted networks and relying solely on the security group for protection.

The master username is the default 'admin' and the password is supplied via var.password, which is also interpolated into EC2 user data; credentials are stored in plaintext in Terraform state rather than managed via Secrets Manager or manage_master_user_password.
The instance uses a parameter group that does not set require_secure_transport (or equivalent), so MySQL connections from the app server may be made in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group only configures character sets and omits require_secure_transport = 1, permitting unencrypted client connections to the database.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance profile full control over all buckets, instances and databases in the account; combined with an internet-reachable web server this is a direct privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration path via the instance metadata service.

The user_data script embeds the RDS master username and var.password in cleartext, writing them to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; user data is retrievable from the instance metadata endpoint by anyone with SSRF or shell access on the host.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; an SSRF flaw in the PHP application would allow retrieval of the highly privileged instance-profile credentials and the plaintext DB password in user data.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume containing the credential file dbinfo.inc is stored unencrypted.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, permitting unrestricted outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control if the database host is compromised.

findings.issue_category: missing rule descriptions and open defaults
findings.description: The RDS security group is defined with no explicit description on rules and is paired with a publicly accessible database, so the only control preventing internet access to port 3306 is the separately managed rule set; any additional permissive rule immediately exposes MySQL.

findings.issue_category: deletion protection and audit logging disabled
findings.description: skip_final_snapshot = true with no deletion_protection and no enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error logs) means the database can be destroyed without a snapshot and provides no security audit trail.
The database endpoint is emitted as an unmasked Terraform output alongside a publicly accessible instance, exposing the connection target to anyone with access to state or CI logs.
